plain.en-IN: Your business
plain.hi-IN: Aapka business

terms.definition: One legally distinct business whose books, stock and filings are kept completely separate from every other business in the product. Every record in the product belongs to exactly one company.
terms.example: Sharma Fruit Traders and Sharma Logistics are two companies even if the same person owns both.

plain.en-IN: A shop, godown or office of your business
plain.hi-IN: Aapke business ki dukaan, godown ya office

terms.definition: A place of business inside one company. Branches share the company's books but can have their own invoice number series, stock location and users.
terms.example: Karol Bagh shop and Narela godown are two branches of one company.

plain.en-IN: A customer or a supplier
plain.hi-IN: Customer ya supplier

terms.definition: Any external person or business you buy from or sell to. A party can be a customer, a supplier, or both.
terms.example: ABC Traders buys apples from you and also sells you crates, so ABC Traders is one party with both roles.

plain.en-IN: Someone who buys from you
plain.hi-IN: Jo aapse kharidta hai

terms.definition: A party in the role of buyer. Amounts a customer has not yet paid you are receivables.
terms.example: ABC Traders bought 70 boxes of apples and still owes Rs 50,000.

plain.en-IN: Someone you buy from
plain.hi-IN: Jisse aap kharidte hain

terms.definition: A party in the role of seller to you. Amounts you have not yet paid a supplier are payables.
terms.example: Nashik Farms sold you 100 boxes of apples and you still owe Rs 80,000.

plain.en-IN: A thing you buy or sell
plain.hi-IN: Jo cheez aap bechte ya kharidte hain

terms.definition: A good or a service you trade in, with a stock-keeping unit, a base unit of measure and a tax classification (HSN for goods, SAC for services).
terms.example: Apple Box 10kg, HSN 0808, base unit BOX.

plain.en-IN: How you count the item
plain.hi-IN: Item kis mein ginte hain

terms.definition: The countable unit for an item, for example BOX, KG, PCS, LTR. Alternate units convert to the base unit using a fixed, recorded factor.
terms.example: 1 BOX = 10 KG, so selling 7 BOX reduces 70 KG of stock.

plain.en-IN: One money entry in your books
plain.hi-IN: Hisaab ki ek entry

terms.definition: A single, balanced financial event recorded in the ledger. Every voucher has a type (sale, purchase, receipt, payment, journal, credit note, debit note), a date, a company, and two or more journal lines whose debits equal credits.
terms.example: Finalising a Rs 1,180 sale creates one sale voucher with three lines: customer +1,180 debit, sales 1,000 credit, output GST 180 credit.

plain.en-IN: One line of a money entry
plain.hi-IN: Entry ki ek line

terms.definition: One debit or credit against one account inside a voucher. A line never exists outside a voucher and is never edited after the voucher is final.
terms.example: Output CGST 90.00 credit is one journal line of a sale voucher.

plain.en-IN: Every entry has two sides that must match
plain.hi-IN: Har entry ke do pehlu, dono barabar

terms.definition: The rule that the total of debits equals the total of credits in every voucher. The product refuses to post a voucher that does not balance to zero.
terms.example: Money went to the customer's account (debit 1,180) and came from sales (1,000) plus tax owed to government (180).

plain.en-IN: Value coming in or owed to you
plain.hi-IN: Aapko milne wala / aata hua

terms.definition: The left side of an entry. Debits increase assets and expenses and decrease income, liabilities and equity.
terms.example: When ABC Traders owes you Rs 1,180, their account is debited by Rs 1,180.

plain.en-IN: Value going out or owed by you
plain.hi-IN: Aapse jaane wala / aapka dena

terms.definition: The right side of an entry. Credits increase income, liabilities and equity and decrease assets and expenses.
terms.example: Sales income of Rs 1,000 is credited when you raise the invoice.

plain.en-IN: A named pocket in your books
plain.hi-IN: Hisaab ka ek khaana

terms.definition: A named bucket that collects journal lines, such as Cash, Bank, Sales, Purchases, Output CGST, or one specific customer. Every account has a type that decides its normal side.
terms.example: Cash in hand, HDFC Current Account, Sales - Goods.

plain.en-IN: The list of all pockets in your books
plain.hi-IN: Sabhi khaaton ki list

terms.definition: The complete, company-specific tree of accounts with their types and codes. The product seeds an India-ready default chart during onboarding, which the business may extend.
terms.example: 1000 Assets > 1100 Cash and Bank > 1110 Cash in hand.

plain.en-IN: What kind of pocket it is
plain.hi-IN: Khaate ka prakaar

terms.definition: One of ASSET, LIABILITY, EQUITY, INCOME, EXPENSE. The type fixes the normal balance side and where the account appears in reports.
terms.example: Sales is INCOME, so it normally has a credit balance and appears in profit and loss.

plain.en-IN: What kind of entry it is
plain.hi-IN: Entry ka prakaar

terms.definition: One of SALE, PURCHASE, RECEIPT, PAYMENT, JOURNAL, CREDIT_NOTE, DEBIT_NOTE, OPENING_BALANCE, REVERSAL. The type decides which posting template and permissions apply.
terms.example: Money received from a customer is a RECEIPT, not a SALE.

plain.en-IN: The bill you give a customer
plain.hi-IN: Customer ko diya gaya bill

terms.definition: The legal document for a sale. When finalised it gets a permanent number, reduces stock, records tax payable and creates a receivable from the customer.
terms.example: Invoice INV/2026-27/00042 to ABC Traders for 70 boxes of apples.

plain.en-IN: The bill your supplier gives you
plain.hi-IN: Supplier se aaya bill

terms.definition: A supplier's bill that you record. When approved it increases stock, records input tax credit and creates a payable to the supplier. It never creates a sale.
terms.example: Nashik Farms bill NF/1187 for 100 boxes of apples increases stock by 100 boxes.

plain.en-IN: You return money or value to a customer
plain.hi-IN: Customer ko wapas dena

terms.definition: A document that reduces what a customer owes you, used for sales returns, rate reductions and post-sale discounts. It reverses income, tax and, when goods come back, stock.
terms.example: ABC Traders returned 10 boxes, so a credit note reduces their dues by the value of 10 boxes plus tax.

plain.en-IN: You reduce what you owe a supplier
plain.hi-IN: Supplier ko kam dena

terms.definition: A document that reduces what you owe a supplier, used for purchase returns, rate corrections and rejected goods.
terms.example: You returned 5 damaged boxes to Nashik Farms and raised a debit note.

plain.en-IN: Money customers still owe you
plain.hi-IN: Customer se lena baaki

terms.definition: The unpaid balance of finalised sales invoices after subtracting accepted payments, credit notes and approved write-offs.
terms.example: Customer still owes Rs 50,000 on a Rs 1,00,000 invoice after paying Rs 50,000.

plain.en-IN: Money you still owe suppliers
plain.hi-IN: Supplier ko dena baaki

terms.definition: The unpaid balance of approved purchase invoices after subtracting payments made, debit notes and approved adjustments.
terms.example: You still owe Nashik Farms Rs 30,000.

plain.en-IN: Linking a payment to the bills it settles
plain.hi-IN: Payment ko bill se jodna

terms.definition: The recorded link between a payment and one or more invoices, with the exact amount applied to each. Unallocated money stays visible as on-account balance instead of being guessed.
terms.example: A Rs 50,000 cheque is allocated Rs 30,000 to invoice 41 and Rs 20,000 to invoice 42.

plain.en-IN: Money received but not yet matched to a bill
plain.hi-IN: Paisa aaya, bill se jodna baaki

terms.definition: A payment held against a party without being applied to specific invoices. The product never guesses which invoice it settles.
terms.example: ABC paid Rs 10,000 in advance before any invoice existed.

plain.en-IN: How long money has been due
plain.hi-IN: Kitne dinon se baaki hai

terms.definition: A breakdown of outstanding balances into age buckets counted from the due date, for example 0-30, 31-60, 61-90 and over 90 days.
terms.example: Rs 20,000 of ABC's dues is more than 90 days old.

plain.en-IN: A month or year of your books
plain.hi-IN: Hisaab ka mahina ya saal

terms.definition: A dated window of the books that can be open, soft-locked or hard-locked. India's financial year runs 1 April to 31 March and is named like 2026-27.
terms.example: April 2026 belongs to financial year 2026-27.

plain.en-IN: Closing old months so they cannot change
plain.hi-IN: Purane mahine band karna

terms.definition: A control that prevents new or changed postings dated inside a closed period. A soft lock can be overridden by an authorised user with a recorded reason; a hard lock cannot be overridden at all.
terms.example: After GST for April is filed, April is hard-locked and a backdated sale is refused.

plain.en-IN: What you already had when you started using the app
plain.hi-IN: App shuru karte waqt jo pehle se tha

terms.definition: The balances of accounts, parties and stock carried into the product on the go-live date, posted as a single balanced opening voucher.
terms.example: On 1 April 2026 you already had Rs 2,00,000 cash and ABC owed you Rs 40,000.

plain.en-IN: Undoing an entry by making an opposite entry
plain.hi-IN: Ulti entry se sudhaarna

terms.definition: The only way to undo a final voucher. A new voucher with mirrored debits and credits is posted and both vouchers stay visible forever. Nothing is deleted.
terms.example: A wrongly posted Rs 5,000 payment is reversed on 12 May and the correct entry is posted separately.

plain.en-IN: Replacing an entry with a corrected version
plain.hi-IN: Sudhaari hui entry se badalna

terms.definition: A controlled correction that reverses the original voucher and posts a corrected one, keeping both linked to the same source document and to each other.
terms.example: The invoice had the wrong rate; the amendment reverses it and posts the corrected invoice with a new version number.

plain.en-IN: The permanent record of who did what and when
plain.hi-IN: Kisne kya kab kiya, ka permanent record

terms.definition: An append-only history of material actions with actor, timestamp, inputs, outputs, decision and any override reason. Secrets are never written into it.
terms.example: Priya finalised invoice 42 at 11:04 on 12 May 2026 and overrode the credit limit with the reason 'owner approved on call'.

plain.en-IN: A tag that stops the same action happening twice
plain.hi-IN: Ek hi kaam do baar hone se rokne wala tag

terms.definition: A caller-supplied unique key for a command. If the same key is sent again, the product returns the original result instead of creating a second record.
terms.example: The app retries after a network failure; the invoice is created once, not twice.

plain.en-IN: The list of things the app could not decide safely
plain.hi-IN: Jo app khud tay nahin kar saka, uski list

terms.definition: A worklist of transactions the product refused to complete because a fact was missing, confidence was low or facts contradicted each other. Items wait for a person; they are never auto-posted.
terms.example: The place of supply is missing, so the invoice waits in the exception queue instead of guessing IGST or CGST.

plain.en-IN: A person saying yes before something important happens
plain.hi-IN: Zaroori kaam se pehle kisi ki haan

terms.definition: A required human decision, with permissions and a preview, before a sensitive action such as finalising an invoice, overriding stock or filing a return.
terms.example: The manager approves a sale that exceeds the customer's credit limit.

plain.en-IN: Going ahead despite a warning, with a recorded reason
plain.hi-IN: Warning ke baawajood aage badhna, kaaran likhkar

terms.definition: An authorised decision to proceed past a warning or block. It always requires a permission, a typed reason and an audit entry. Some blocks cannot be overridden at all.
terms.example: Selling below the negative-stock limit is overridden by the owner with the reason 'goods received, bill pending'.

plain.en-IN: The 15-character GST number of a business
plain.hi-IN: Business ka 15 akshar ka GST number

terms.definition: The Goods and Services Tax Identification Number. The first two characters are the state code, the next ten are the PAN, and the last is a checksum character the product validates.
terms.example: 07AABCU9603R1ZM is registered in Delhi (state code 07).

plain.en-IN: The 10-character income-tax number
plain.hi-IN: 10 akshar ka income tax number

terms.definition: Permanent Account Number issued by the income-tax department. It is embedded inside a GSTIN.
terms.example: AABCU9603R.

plain.en-IN: The government's code for a type of goods
plain.hi-IN: Saaman ka sarkari code

terms.definition: Harmonised System of Nomenclature code that classifies goods for GST. The number of digits you must print depends on your turnover.
terms.example: Fresh apples are HSN 0808.

plain.en-IN: The government's code for a type of service
plain.hi-IN: Service ka sarkari code

terms.definition: Services Accounting Code that classifies services for GST.
terms.example: Goods transport by road is SAC 9965.

plain.en-IN: The state the sale counts as happening in
plain.hi-IN: Bikri kis rajya ki maani jayegi

terms.definition: The state whose GST applies to a supply, decided by deterministic rules from the type of supply and the recipient's details. It decides whether CGST+SGST or IGST applies. It is never guessed.
terms.example: Goods delivered to a Haryana address from Delhi have Haryana as the place of supply, so IGST applies.

plain.en-IN: The central government's half of GST on a sale inside your state
plain.hi-IN: Apne rajya ki bikri par kendra ka hissa

terms.definition: Central Goods and Services Tax, charged together with SGST or UTGST when the supplier and the place of supply are in the same state or union territory.
terms.example: On a Rs 1,000 intra-state sale at 18 percent, CGST is Rs 90.

plain.en-IN: The state government's half of GST on a sale inside your state
plain.hi-IN: Apne rajya ki bikri par rajya ka hissa

terms.definition: State Goods and Services Tax, charged with CGST on supplies inside one state.
terms.example: On a Rs 1,000 intra-state sale at 18 percent, SGST is Rs 90.

plain.en-IN: The union-territory version of SGST
plain.hi-IN: Union territory ke liye SGST jaisa

terms.definition: Union Territory Goods and Services Tax, charged with CGST for supplies inside a union territory without its own legislature.
terms.example: A supply within Chandigarh uses CGST and UTGST.

plain.en-IN: One combined GST for a sale to another state
plain.hi-IN: Dusre rajya ki bikri par ek hi GST

terms.definition: Integrated Goods and Services Tax, charged as a single amount when the supplier's state and the place of supply differ, and on imports and supplies treated as inter-state.
terms.example: On a Rs 1,000 inter-state sale at 18 percent, IGST is Rs 180.

plain.en-IN: An extra tax on some specific goods
plain.hi-IN: Kuch khaas saaman par extra tax

terms.definition: GST compensation cess charged in addition to GST on notified goods, either as a percentage, a fixed amount per unit, or the higher of the two.
terms.example: Aerated drinks carry cess over and above the GST rate.

plain.en-IN: The amount tax is calculated on
plain.hi-IN: Jis rakam par tax lagta hai

terms.definition: The value of the supply after discounts and before GST. Freight and other charges that form part of the supply are included in it.
terms.example: 70 boxes at Rs 800 less 5 percent discount gives a taxable value of Rs 53,200.

plain.en-IN: The total the customer must pay
plain.hi-IN: Customer ko kitna dena hai

terms.definition: Taxable value plus all GST and cess plus any non-taxable charges, after round-off.
terms.example: Taxable value Rs 1,000 plus GST Rs 180 gives an invoice value of Rs 1,180.

plain.en-IN: The price already contains GST
plain.hi-IN: Rate mein GST shaamil hai

terms.definition: A rate that already includes GST. The product works the tax backwards out of it using a fixed formula and shows both the taxable value and the tax.
terms.example: Rs 118 inclusive at 18 percent means Rs 100 taxable value and Rs 18 GST.

plain.en-IN: You pay the GST instead of your supplier
plain.hi-IN: GST supplier ke bajaay aap bharte hain

terms.definition: A treatment where the recipient, not the supplier, must pay GST to the government on notified supplies or purchases from unregistered persons.
terms.example: Freight from an unregistered goods transport agency may make you liable to pay GST directly.

plain.en-IN: GST you already paid on purchases that reduces your GST bill
plain.hi-IN: Kharid par diya GST jo aapka GST kam karta hai

terms.definition: Credit for GST paid on business purchases, which is set off against GST collected on sales, subject to eligibility conditions and the supplier having reported the invoice.
terms.example: Rs 18,000 GST paid on purchases reduces Rs 30,000 GST collected to Rs 12,000 payable.

plain.en-IN: GST you collected from customers
plain.hi-IN: Customer se liya GST

terms.definition: GST charged on your sales and held as a liability until it is paid to the government.
terms.example: The Rs 180 GST on a Rs 1,180 invoice is output tax.

plain.en-IN: The month or quarter a return covers
plain.hi-IN: Return kis mahine ya quarter ka hai

terms.definition: The GST return period a transaction falls into, decided by its document date and the company's filing frequency.
terms.example: An invoice dated 30 April 2026 belongs to the April 2026 tax period for a monthly filer.

plain.en-IN: The monthly or quarterly list of your sales sent to the GST portal
plain.hi-IN: Apni bikri ki list jo GST portal par jaati hai

terms.definition: The outward-supply return that reports your sales invoices, credit notes and debit notes for a tax period.
terms.example: April's 42 sales invoices are reported in April's GSTR-1.

plain.en-IN: The summary return where you pay GST
plain.hi-IN: Summary return jismein GST bharte hain

terms.definition: The summary return that declares total outward tax, input tax credit claimed and the net GST paid for a tax period.
terms.example: April's GSTR-3B shows Rs 30,000 output tax less Rs 18,000 credit, so Rs 12,000 is paid.

plain.en-IN: The government's statement of purchases your suppliers reported
plain.hi-IN: Supplier ne jo bill report kiye, unki sarkari list

terms.definition: A static, auto-drafted statement of input tax credit available for a tax period, generated from what your suppliers filed. It is compared with your own purchase records.
terms.example: One supplier did not file, so their Rs 9,000 credit is not in GSTR-2B and is held back.

plain.en-IN: An invoice registered with the government portal
plain.hi-IN: Sarkari portal par registered invoice

terms.definition: An invoice whose details are reported to the Invoice Registration Portal, which returns an Invoice Reference Number and a signed QR code. A styled PDF is not an e-invoice by itself.
terms.example: Invoice 42 received IRN 6f2c... and a QR code that must be printed.

plain.en-IN: The government's unique reference for a registered invoice
plain.hi-IN: Registered invoice ka sarkari unique number

terms.definition: Invoice Reference Number returned by the Invoice Registration Portal. Generating it twice for the same invoice is a duplicate the product must prevent.
terms.example: IRN is printed with the QR code on the invoice.

plain.en-IN: The government permit needed to move goods
plain.hi-IN: Maal le jaane ka sarkari permit

terms.definition: An electronic document required for the movement of goods above notified value and distance conditions, carrying transporter and vehicle details and a validity period.
terms.example: Moving Rs 80,000 of apples to another state generally needs an e-way bill before the truck leaves.

plain.en-IN: One in or out of goods
plain.hi-IN: Maal ka ek aana ya jaana

terms.definition: An append-only record of quantity entering or leaving a warehouse for an item, batch and unit, always linked to its source document. Stock on hand is the sum of movements, never a stored number that is edited.
terms.example: Purchase of 100 boxes is one movement in; sale of 70 boxes is one movement out; 30 remain.

plain.en-IN: How much you can still sell right now
plain.hi-IN: Abhi kitna bech sakte hain

terms.definition: Physical quantity minus quantity reserved by drafts and pending approvals. Sales are checked against available quantity, not physical quantity.
terms.example: 100 boxes physically present with 70 reserved by a pending invoice leaves 30 available.

plain.en-IN: How much is actually lying in the godown
plain.hi-IN: Godown mein asal mein kitna hai

terms.definition: The quantity actually held, derived from posted stock movements only.
terms.example: 100 boxes are in the godown even though 70 are promised to a customer.

plain.en-IN: Stock held aside for a draft bill
plain.hi-IN: Draft bill ke liye rakha gaya maal

terms.definition: A temporary hold on quantity created when a sale is drafted or sent for approval, released on cancellation, expiry or conversion to a posted movement.
terms.example: A draft invoice for 70 boxes reserves them so a second user cannot sell the same 70.

plain.en-IN: A specific lot of the same item
plain.hi-IN: Ek hi item ka alag lot

terms.definition: A tracked group of units of an item sharing a lot number, manufacture or expiry date. Batches keep cost and expiry separate within one item.
terms.example: Apple boxes from 2 May expire earlier than those from 9 May.

plain.en-IN: A place where stock is kept
plain.hi-IN: Jahan maal rakha hai

terms.definition: A stock location belonging to a company and usually to a branch. Stock balances are always per warehouse.
terms.example: Narela godown and the shop counter are two warehouses.

plain.en-IN: The most a customer may owe you at one time
plain.hi-IN: Customer se zyada se zyada kitna baaki rakh sakte hain

terms.definition: A per-customer ceiling on total outstanding plus pending transactions. Crossing it warns or blocks according to policy and can only be overridden with permission and a reason.
terms.example: ABC's limit is Rs 1,00,000 and a new Rs 60,000 invoice on Rs 50,000 outstanding crosses it.

plain.en-IN: The few paise added or removed to reach a neat total
plain.hi-IN: Total seedha karne ke liye chhota adjustment

terms.definition: The small difference posted to a dedicated account so the invoice total reaches the configured rounding, keeping the voucher balanced.
terms.example: Rs 1,179.60 is shown as Rs 1,180 with Rs 0.40 posted to round-off.

plain.en-IN: Which version of the rulebook decided this
plain.hi-IN: Kis version ke niyam se faisla hua

terms.definition: The identifier of the deterministic rule set used for a decision, stored with the decision so the same result can be reproduced later.
terms.example: The e-way decision on 12 May 2026 used rule set gst-ewb 2026.04.01.

plain.en-IN: The date from which a rule or rate applies
plain.hi-IN: Niyam ya rate kis taarikh se laagu hai

terms.definition: The date range for which a rate, threshold or rule is valid. Transactions are always evaluated with the rule effective on their own document date.
terms.example: A rate change from 1 July does not change a bill dated 30 June.

plain.en-IN: A person who logs in to the app
plain.hi-IN: App mein login karne wala vyakti

terms.definition: A person with a login who acts inside one or more companies. A user has roles and permissions per company and every action they take is recorded against them.
terms.example: Priya is a billing user at the Karol Bagh shop and can create invoices but not reopen a closed month.

plain.en-IN: A price offer, not a bill
plain.hi-IN: Rate ka offer, bill nahin

terms.definition: A priced offer sent to a customer before a sale. It creates no entry in the books, no tax liability and no stock movement, and it may be converted into a sales invoice.
terms.example: You quote ABC Traders Rs 800 per box; nothing is recorded in your books until they order.

plain.en-IN: A draft bill sent before payment
plain.hi-IN: Payment se pehle bheja gaya draft bill

terms.definition: A document that looks like an invoice and is used to request advance payment, but is not a tax invoice. It creates no ledger entry, no tax liability and no invoice number in the legal series.
terms.example: You send a proforma for Rs 1,00,000 so the customer can arrange the transfer before dispatch.
